Colors and typography
Reference for DTCG color objects, alpha, typography tokens, and dashed borders.
Design Token
wave token --help
Local CLI
## Colors and alpha

Prefer DTCG color objects to describe colors:

```yaml
primary:
  main:
    $value:
      colorSpace: oklch
      components: [0.518, 0.251, 262.6]
      hex: "#0052f5"
```

`hex` is a 6-digit fallback for compatibility output. Put transparency in `alpha`, never inside `hex`.

One build can output CSS and Sketch at the same time. CSS follows `colorSpace`; Sketch outputs `#RRGGBBAA`.

The legacy syntax keeps working. Color and transparency can be written separately, and both `color` and `alpha` accept references:

```yaml
inverse:
  surface:
    $description: Inverted background, commonly used for Snackbar or Toast
    $value:
      color: "{tailwindcss.color.slate.900}"
      alpha: "{wave.dimension.alpha.800}"
```

At build time, Wave resolves references first and then outputs the final color per `colorSpace`.

## Typography

A standard DTCG `typography` value must contain `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `letterSpacing`, and a unit-less number `lineHeight`. `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, and `letterSpacing` each follow their corresponding standard types and may reference tokens of matching types. Extra fields fail the build.

Wave provides flat `$extensions.typography`, an optional `$value.color`, and `lineHeight` with a `px | pt | rem` unit. The typography extension can only be written on a group whose effective `$type` is `typography`, and accepts exactly six sibling fields — `baseFontSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing` — declaring at least one. The legacy nested `typography.defaults` form is rejected; move its fields under `typography`.

The five standard fields act as defaults for child tokens: child groups shallow-override ancestor defaults per field, and the token's own `$value` overrides last; object fields are replaced wholesale with no deep merge. After merging, every typography token must contain the five standard fields. The optional `color` can only be written in the token `$value`, not as an extension default field; JSON/JSONC keep it, CSS additionally emits `-- -color`, and when it directly references an already-emitted `theme.color.*` it stays as `var(-- )`.

`fontSize` is the font size default of a typography composite; `baseFontSize` is only the rem conversion base — they are not the same setting. rem defaults to a `16px` base. To override it, declare a finite number greater than 0, or a reference resolving to such a number, in `theme.font.$extensions.typography.baseFontSize`; the value is interpreted in CSS px and cannot be a dimension object. The base itself is never included in the typography JSON/JSONC value. With rem in play, CSS writes a valid `font-size` on `:root` and keeps the token's rem values; Sketch converts `fontSize`, absolute `lineHeight`, and `letterSpacing` as `rem × effective base`. `fontSize` and `letterSpacing` keep up to three decimal places; the final `lineHeight` always rounds up to an integer.

```yaml
theme:
  font:
    $type: typography
    $extensions:
      typography:
        baseFontSize: 14
        fontFamily: ["Inter", "sans-serif"]
        fontSize:
          value: 0.875
          unit: rem
        fontWeight: 400
        letterSpacing: 0
    body:
      $value:
        lineHeight: 1.5
    label:
      $value:
        lineHeight:
          value: 20
          unit: px
```

### Adjust the rem base per profile

A profile cannot re-declare the extensions of an existing group. When different profiles need different bases, make `baseFontSize` in main reference a registered number token, then override that token's value by ID in the profile.

Base file `main.yaml`:

```yaml
$id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    platform: [json, css, sketch]
theme:
  font:
    $type: typography
    $extensions:
      typography:
        baseFontSize: "{theme.font.base-size}"
        fontFamily: ["Inter", "sans-serif"]
        fontSize: { value: 1, unit: rem }
        fontWeight: 400
        lineHeight: 1.5
        letterSpacing: 0
    base-size:
      $id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
      $type: number
      $value: 14
    body:
      $value: {}
```

Delta file `profiles/mobile.yaml`:

```yaml
$config:
  base: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
$override:
  bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb:
    $value: 16
```

After running `wave token build -f ./profiles/mobile.yaml`, the body font size is still `1rem`; the CSS root font size is `16px` and the Sketch font size is `16`. main's base stays `14`. See [Profiles and Night](/design-token/quality-theming) for profile identity and the full override rules.

### Font and line-height output

`fontFamily` accepts one string or a string array. The DTCG schema keeps the standard structure; the CSS platform requires the value to form a non-empty font stack. CSS turns arrays into a legal font stack: plain CSS identifiers are unquoted; other names lose one layer of existing paired quotes, then get wrapped in double quotes with escaping. `inherit`, `initial`, `unset`, `revert`, and `revert-layer` are always quoted. A typography token in CSS only emits field variables (`-family`, `-size`, `-weight`, `-line-height`, `-letter-spacing`, and optionally `-color`), never an aggregate shorthand variable. When an already-emitted `fontFamily` token equals the typography's font stack, CSS omits the local `-- -family` field variable and consumers take the family token's own variable; without an equal-value token, the local `-- -family` is still emitted. Sketch does not resolve system aliases; when the array contains `PingFang SC` it is preferred, otherwise the first concrete font is chosen. `system`, `system-ui`, `-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, and CSS generic families are not concrete fonts; when the array contains only those, Sketch omits `fontFamily`. String values keep the existing behavior.

`lineHeight` must be greater than 0. A unit-less number or a numeric string means a multiplier; `{ value }` does not mean a multiplier and must carry a unit. CSS keeps multipliers and absolute units; Sketch's final `lineHeight` rounds up to an integer regardless of multiplier, `px`, `pt`, or `rem`. `fontSize`, absolute `lineHeight`, and `letterSpacing` use a rem base of 16 by default, overridable via `theme.font.$extensions.typography.baseFontSize`. Wave never converts between px and pt.

### Sketch color output

In Sketch output, every color asset's `color` field is an `#RRGGBBAA` HEX8 snapshot; colors with alpha or opacity overrides fold transparency into the snapshot's alpha channel. Color positions inside layer assets (`shadows[].color`, `gradient.color`) are HEX8 snapshots too, with no Swatch binding: whether a color token registers `$id` or is skipped by `sketch.skip` only affects whether it appears as a color asset in the manifest, never the values at color positions.

The gap layer of an outline is fixed to `#ffffffff`. The legacy `@/ ` string references and the trial `{ "$ref": " " }` bindings are no longer emitted; changing colors on the Sketch side requires re-importing the payload.

## Dashed borders

`border` is a standard composite of `color`, `width`, and `style`. `style` accepts a standard stroke style string, an object with `dashArray` and `lineCap`, or a reference to a standalone `strokeStyle` token:

```yaml
antline:
  $type: border
  $value:
    color: "{theme.color.primary}"
    width: 1
    style:
      dashArray:
        - value: 4
          unit: px
        - value: 8
          unit: px
      lineCap: butt
```

String styles support `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `outset`, and `inset`. An object style must contain both a non-empty `dashArray` and a `lineCap`; `lineCap` accepts only `round`, `butt`, `square`. `dashArray` members follow the dimension contract and also accept Wave dimension shorthands and extended units. Odd-length arrays repeat once; every platform outputs the same even-length array.

The DTCG schema does not restrict dash member signs or all-zero combinations; when CSS cannot express a negative or all-zero pattern, it shows the token path, type, and value shape, then fails. CSS outputs a usable `dashed` shorthand for object styles plus `-dash-array` and `-line-cap` companion variables, e.g. `--border-antline: 1px dashed #1872f0`, `--border-antline-dash-array: 4px 8px`, and `--border-antline-line-cap: butt`. A companion name colliding with a real token key fails the build. Sketch output contains only syncable assets; dashed borders produce no Sketch record.

pages.title: Extensions and output
pages.description: Reference for `$extensions` fields and the json, jsonc, css, sketch, and md-yml output formats.
pages.body:
## Output formats

| platform | Output file | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json` | `{theme}.json` | Flat JSON |
| `jsonc` | `{theme}.jsonc` | JSONC with comments |
| `css` | `{theme}.css` | CSS variables |
| `sketch` | `{theme}2sketch.json` | Sketch asset manifest (payload v2) |
| `md-yml` | `{theme}2md.yml` | YAML token fragment for Markdown frontmatter |

CSS output covers the `color`, `state`, `shadow`, `gradient`, `border`, `radius`, and `font` roots. `theme.dimension` is no longer a public output root; the build suggests migration, and full recommendations come from `wave token doctor`.

Typography tokens emit field variables in CSS (`-family`, `-size`, `-weight`, `-line-height`, `-letter-spacing`, optionally `-color`) rather than an aggregate shorthand variable, and emit text asset records in Sketch. Border tokens with `$extensions.platform.sketch.outline` emit the outline value and offset companions in CSS, and generate a two-layer shadow that simulates the outline in Sketch.

### Platform output of standard types

JSON and JSONC output flat key/value; dimension and dimension fields inside composites keep their unit strings. md-yml uses the same final values but groups them by namespace. CSS emits directly consumable values. Sketch output is an asset manifest; only syncable assets produce records:

| `$type` | JSON / JSONC | CSS | Sketch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | Target color space string, or a clean DTCG color object | CSS Color 4 value | `kind: color` record with HEX8 color |
| `dimension` | `"8px"` | `8px` | `kind: layer` record when in a radius group or generating a sketch property dimension; otherwise no record |
| `fontFamily` | string or string array | font stack | no record |
| `fontWeight` | number | number | no record (text records only accept 100–900 in hundreds) |
| `duration` | `"200ms"` | `200ms` | no record |
| `cubicBezier` | number array | `cubic-bezier(...)` | no record |
| `number` | number | number | `kind: layer` record when in a radius group or generating a sketch property dimension; otherwise no record |
| `strokeStyle` | string or `{ dashArray, lineCap }` | main variable plus dash/line-cap companions | no record |
| `border` | `{ color, width, style }` | border shorthand plus required companions | only borders with `platform.sketch.outline` generate a `kind: layer` record |
| `transition` | `{ duration, delay, timingFunction }` | transition value | no record |
| `shadow` | Single-layer object or layer array | box-shadow value | `kind: layer` record (`shadows` field) |
| `gradient` | stop array | linear-gradient value | `kind: layer` record (`gradient` field) |
| `typography` | Five standard fields plus optional Wave `color` | field variables | `kind: text` record |

When a platform cannot express an input, Wave stops the build and reports the token path, type, and reason. Typical failures include: a color that CSS or Sketch cannot convert with no `hex` fallback, an empty font family or negative or all-zero dash pattern in CSS, and relative units Sketch native numeric properties cannot represent. For unknown custom `$type`s, CSS accepts scalars only; objects or arrays fail explicitly, and `[object Object]` output is forbidden.

When the current directory has a `main.yaml`, `wave token doctor` checks it by default; pass `wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml` to be explicit.

Multiple platforms are declared in `$config`:

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./dist
    platform: [json, jsonc, css, sketch, md-yml]
```

## md-yml

`md-yml` generates a YAML token fragment that can be copied into Markdown frontmatter. With `filterLayer: 1`, the following tokens produce `{theme}2md.yml`:

```yaml
color:
  primary-main: '#1a72f0'
  primary-on-main: '#ffffff'
  text-emphasis: '#112233'
radius:
  md: 8px
font:
  font-family:
    - system-ui
    - sans-serif
  heading-h1:
    color: "{color.text-emphasis}"
    fontFamily: "{font.font-family}"
    fontSize: 2.5rem
    fontWeight: 700
    letterSpacing: 0px
    lineHeight: 1.2
```

The first output layer is the namespace, and the remaining source path segments join with `-`. So `theme.color.primary.main` becomes `color.primary-main` after filtering `theme`, and document bodies can use:

```markdown
{color.primary-main}
```

md-yml keeps theme direct references that project onto the same file and rewrites their paths to output paths. For example, `theme.font.heading.h1` inherits `fontFamily: "{theme.font.font-family}"` from the flat fields of `theme.font.$extensions.typography` and outputs as `fontFamily: "{font.font-family}"`. Direct references inside complete tokens, composite sub-fields, and array members follow the same rule.

A reference survives only when the target is also emitted into the current payload and the consumer slot is not rewritten by computation. External resource references, `$ref` + override, `smoothShadow` / `smoothGradient`, `inheritColor` / `currentColor`, and other computed values still output the final value after resolver and transformer processing. Objects, arrays, and explicit composites keep their structure. The file contains no `---` delimiter, `$description` comments, token wrappers, or `$type` / `$value` metadata.

After `filterLayer` processing, at least a namespace and a local key must remain. Source segments in the path cannot be empty or contain `.`; when different source paths project onto the same key, the build fails. The build also fails before writing any product of that pass when a value contains data YAML cannot represent losslessly, such as `undefined`, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays, or cycles.

## $extensions

`$extensions` expresses Wave's extension semantics. After the build, extension fields are consumed and never appear verbatim in output files.

Profiles inherit base tokens and the extensions of existing groups; re-declaring or overriding them is not allowed. `$override` replaces `$value` only and cannot change extension settings like `smoothShadow.target`, `platform.sketch.path`, or `inheritColor.property.opacity`. When those differences are needed, create a separate base directory; new tokens can declare their own extensions. Full boundaries: [Profiles and Night](/design-token/quality-theming).

Supported fields:

| Field | Location | Applicable types | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `typography` | group | effective type `typography` | Font default fields and rem base; see [Colors and typography](/design-token/color-typography) |
| `smoothShadow` | token | `shadow` | Derive a multi-layer smooth shadow from a single layer |
| `smoothGradient` | token | `gradient` | Derive a smooth gradient from 2 stops |
| `inheritColor` | token | `color` | Emit a context-inheriting color |
| `platform.sketch.path` | group or token | any token | Adjust the grouping prefix of Sketch asset names |
| `platform.sketch.skip` | group or token | any token | Skip Sketch output only |
| `platform.sketch.property.opacity` | token | `number` under `theme.state.*` | Emit the Sketch opacity field |
| `platform.sketch.property.cornerRadius` | token | radius/dimension tokens | Emit the Sketch corners.radii field |
| `platform.sketch.outline` | border token | `border` | Emit a CSS outline and the Sketch two-layer shadow simulation |
| `composite` | group | direct children must be tokens | Merge a group of tokens into a component object |
| `currentColor` | token | legacy | Legacy compatibility field; new content uses `inheritColor` |

The legacy forms `$extensions.sketch.*` and `$extensions.outline` are rejected outright by the build, which points to the migration command. One run in the project directory completes the rename (preview only by default; add `--write` to write back):

```bash
wave token migrate extensions --write
```

## smoothShadow

`smoothShadow` applies to `shadow` tokens, deriving a multi-layer smooth shadow from a single layer.

```yaml
theme:
  shadow:
    $type: shadow
    card:
      $value:
        color: "#00000033"
        offsetX: 0
        offsetY: 8
        blur: 24
        spread: 0
      $extensions:
        smoothShadow:
          cubicBezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]
          step: 4
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cubicBezier` | 4 numbers, or a curve referenced from a dimension resource |
| `step` | Number of visible output layers, integer `>= 1` |
| `target` | Optional target shadow layer; when present, interpolates from the current shadow to the target |

The input value must be a single shadow layer object, not an array. With `target`, `step` must be `>= 2`.

`target` accepts the same fields as a shadow layer, and can specify the target transparency alone through `alpha`:

```yaml
$extensions:
  smoothShadow:
    cubicBezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]
    step: 4
    target:
      alpha: 0.08
      offsetX: 0
      offsetY: 16
      blur: 48
      spread: -4
```

## smoothGradient

`smoothGradient` applies to `gradient` tokens, expanding 2 endpoints into multiple gradient stops.

```yaml
theme:
  gradient:
    $type: gradient
    overlay:
      $value:
        - color: "#00000000"
          position: 0
        - color: "#000000cc"
          position: 1
      $extensions:
        smoothGradient:
          cubicBezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]
          step: 7
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cubicBezier` | 4 numbers, or a curve referenced from a dimension resource |
| `step` | Total stop count, integer `>= 2` |

The input gradient must have exactly 2 stops.

## inheritColor

`inheritColor` applies to `color` tokens, meaning the output inherits the context color.

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    icon:
      $value: "#000000"
      $extensions:
        inheritColor: true
    iconSubtle:
      $value: "#000000"
      $extensions:
        inheritColor:
          property:
            opacity: 0.36
          siblingSlot: foreground
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `inheritColor: true` | Emit an inheriting color |
| `property.opacity` | Emit opacity; supports numbers, aliases, `$ref` |
| `property.alpha` | Emit alpha; supports numbers, aliases, `$ref` |
| `siblingSlot` | In Sketch output, find the sibling color value within the same composite |

Output differences:

| Platform | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `css` | `currentColor` or `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor X%, transparent)` |
| `json` / `jsonc` / `md-yml` | `$COLOR_FOREGROUND` or `{ color: "$COLOR_FOREGROUND", opacity: X }` |
| `sketch` | Writes Sketch color, `opacity`, or `alpha` fields |

## platform.sketch

`$extensions.platform.sketch` only controls Sketch JSON output and does not affect the keys of `json`, `jsonc`, `css`, or `md-yml`. `path` and `skip` can be written on a group or a token; on a group, they apply to descendant tokens.

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    $extensions:
      platform:
        sketch:
          path: foundation/color
    primary:
      $value: "#1872f0"
  state:
    hover:
      $type: number
      $value: 0.16
      $extensions:
        platform:
          sketch:
            path: foundation/interaction
            property:
              opacity: true
  radius:
    card:
      $type: dimension
      $value: "12px"
      $extensions:
        platform:
          sketch:
            property:
              cornerRadius: true
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `platform.sketch.path` | Slash grouping prefix of Sketch asset names, e.g. `foundation/color`; can be written on a group or a token |
| `platform.sketch.skip` | When `true`, omits Sketch output; a descendant group or token may explicitly write `false` to restore output |
| `platform.sketch.property.opacity` | Writes the `opacity` number in layer records |
| `platform.sketch.property.cornerRadius` | Writes the `corners.radii` number in layer records |
| `platform.sketch.outline` | Border tokens only; generates the two-layer shadow outline simulation per `offset` and makes CSS emit outline variables |

`path` uses slash grouping as the prefix of asset names. Assuming `filterLayer: 1`, the color token above produces an asset named `foundation/color/primary`; without `path`, the name is the leaf key after `filterLayer` processing.

Priority:

1. The token's own `path`
2. The nearest parent group's `path`
3. The `path` of a higher ancestor group

`property` does not inherit. To emit `opacity` or `corners.radii`, it must still be written on the corresponding token.

`skip` accepts booleans only, inherits from the nearest declaration, and the token's own value wins. An explicit `false` overrides an ancestor group's `true`. This switch filters Sketch output only; CSS, JSON, JSONC, and md-yml still emit the token.

Limits:

- `path` must be a plain slash grouping path, e.g. `foundation/color`; leading/trailing slashes, empty segments, and `.` are not allowed.
- `property` supports only `opacity` and `cornerRadius`, the value must be `true`, and it can only be written on tokens.
- `property.opacity` applies to `number` tokens under `theme.state.*`.
- `property.cornerRadius` applies to radius/dimension tokens under `theme.radius.*` or `theme.dimension.*`.
- `outline` takes effect only on border tokens.
- Unknown fields, unknown properties, or misplaced usage fail the build. For example, `$type: number` with `property.fillColor: true` errors because `fillColor` is not a supported Sketch property; `$type: color` with `property.opacity: true` errors because `opacity` only accepts state number tokens.
- Unknown platforms under `platform.*` (e.g. `platform.figma`) only produce warnings and do not affect the build; they are reserved compatibility slots for future platforms.

## Sketch asset manifest

The `sketch` platform outputs a JSON asset manifest: the root holds `meta` and `assets`, with one asset per line inside `assets` for easy human review and git diff.

```json
{
  "meta": { "themeId": "6f1c2a54b7d84e0f9a1c32d45e6b70f8", "baseId": null, "version": 2 },
  "assets": [
    { "uuid": "0f8e6d5c4b3a29180f7e6d5c4b3a2918", "name": "foundation/color/primary-main", "kind": "color", "color": "#1872f0ff" },
    { "name": "foundation/interaction/hover", "kind": "layer", "opacity": 0.16 }
  ]
}
```

- `meta.themeId` comes from the current day document's root `$id`: main output uses main's identity, named profile output uses that profile's own identity; `null` when missing. Use `wave token ids --write` to fill in document identity. Night inherits the corresponding day's identity.
- `meta.baseId` is the main's root `$id` in named profile (including its night) output, and `null` in main (including its night) output. It is a payload v2 addition, and `version` stays fixed at `2`; if the Sketch plugin strictly validates the legacy `meta` field set, confirm the plugin accepts `baseId` first — do not judge compatibility by the version number alone.
- Every record carries `name` and `kind`; when the token has a registered token-level `$id`, it also carries `uuid`, otherwise that field is omitted.
- `kind` has exactly three values: `color` (color tokens, corresponding to Swatches), `text` (typography tokens, corresponding to shared text styles), and `layer` (shadows, gradients, outline borders, corner dimensions, etc., corresponding to shared layer styles).
- Only syncable assets enter the manifest: plain borders, plain dimensions, transitions, and the like produce no records.
- Text records contain only font fields (`fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `kerning`), never the text color; `fontWeight` accepts only the 100–900 hundreds scale, and other values error immediately at Sketch build time, leaving CSS and JSON unaffected.
- Layer records combine fields such as `shadows`, `gradient`, `opacity`, and `corners`; `fills` and `gradient` are mutually exclusive within one record.
- Records follow the token order in the theme files; renaming or changing anything besides `path` does not disturb the order.

Asset names must be unique within one manifest: when two tokens produce exactly the same name, the build errors. Slashes in names are plain characters, and overlapping prefixes are not conflicts — `shadow` and `shadow/elevation-1` can coexist.

Color positions in layer records always carry `#RRGGBBAA` HEX8 color snapshots with no Swatch binding; color assets in the same manifest still carry `uuid` by their own `$id` for Sync Token adoption. Details: [Colors and typography](/design-token/color-typography).

## composite

`composite` merges a group's direct child tokens into one component object. Suited to component variants such as buttons and cards.

```yaml
component:
  button:
    outline:
      $extensions:
        composite: true
      fill:
        $value: "{theme.color.surface}"
      border:
        $value: "{theme.color.primary}"
      radius:
        $value: "9999px"
```

Rules:

- `composite` is written on the group's `$extensions`.
- Direct children of a composite group must all be tokens; further group nesting is not allowed.
- JSON/JSONC/md-yml output merges into an object.
- Sketch output no longer maps composites to component style fields; component logic will be designed separately later.

        spread: 0

| --- | --- |
| `css` | `currentColor` or `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor X%, transparent)` |
| `json` / `jsonc` / `md-yml` | `$COLOR_FOREGROUND` or `{ color: "$COLOR_FOREGROUND", opacity: X }` |
| `sketch` | Writes Sketch color, `opacity`, or `alpha` fields |

## platform.sketch

`$extensions.platform.sketch` only controls Sketch JSON output and does not affect the keys of `json`, `jsonc`, `css`, or `md-yml`. `path` and `skip` can be written on a group or a token; on a group, they apply to descendant tokens.

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    $extensions:
      platform:
        sketch:
          path: foundation/color
    primary:
      $value: "#1872f0"
  state:
    hover:
      $type: number
      $value: 0.16
      $extensions:
        platform:
          sketch:
            path: foundation/interaction
            property:
              opacity: true
  radius:
    card:
      $type: dimension
      $value: "12px"
      $extensions:
        platform:
          sketch:
            property:
              cornerRadius: true
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `platform.sketch.path` | Slash grouping prefix of Sketch asset names, e.g. `foundation/color`; can be written on a group or a token |
| `platform.sketch.skip` | When `true`, omits Sketch output; a descendant group or token may explicitly write `false` to restore output |
| `platform.sketch.property.opacity` | Writes the `opacity` number in layer records |
| `platform.sketch.property.cornerRadius` | Writes the `corners.radii` number in layer records |
| `platform.sketch.outline` | Border tokens only; generates the two-layer shadow outline simulation per `offset` and makes CSS emit outline variables |

`path` uses slash grouping as the prefix of asset names. Assuming `filterLayer: 1`, the color token above produces an asset named `foundation/color/primary`; without `path`, the name is the leaf key after `filterLayer` processing.

Priority:

1. The token's own `path`
2. The nearest parent group's `path`
3. The `path` of a higher ancestor group

`property` does not inherit. To emit `opacity` or `corners.radii`, it must still be written on the corresponding token.

`skip` accepts booleans only, inherits from the nearest declaration, and the token's own value wins. An explicit `false` overrides an ancestor group's `true`. This switch filters Sketch output only; CSS, JSON, JSONC, and md-yml still emit the token.

Limits:

- `path` must be a plain slash grouping path, e.g. `foundation/color`; leading/trailing slashes, empty segments, and `.` are not allowed.
- `property` supports only `opacity` and `cornerRadius`, the value must be `true`, and it can only be written on tokens.
- `property.opacity` applies to `number` tokens under `theme.state.*`.
- `property.cornerRadius` applies to radius/dimension tokens under `theme.radius.*` or `theme.dimension.*`.
- `outline` takes effect only on border tokens.
- Unknown fields, unknown properties, or misplaced usage fail the build. For example, `$type: number` with `property.fillColor: true` errors because `fillColor` is not a supported Sketch property; `$type: color` with `property.opacity: true` errors because `opacity` only accepts state number tokens.
- Unknown platforms under `platform.*` (e.g. `platform.figma`) only produce warnings and do not affect the build; they are reserved compatibility slots for future platforms.

## Sketch asset manifest

The `sketch` platform outputs a JSON asset manifest: the root holds `meta` and `assets`, with one asset per line inside `assets` for easy human review and git diff.

```json
{
  "meta": { "themeId": "6f1c2a54b7d84e0f9a1c32d45e6b70f8", "baseId": null, "version": 2 },
  "assets": [
    { "uuid": "0f8e6d5c4b3a29180f7e6d5c4b3a2918", "name": "foundation/color/primary-main", "kind": "color", "color": "#1872f0ff" },
    { "name": "foundation/interaction/hover", "kind": "layer", "opacity": 0.16 }
  ]
}
```

- `meta.themeId` comes from the current day document's root `$id`: main output uses main's identity, named profile output uses that profile's own identity; `null` when missing. Use `wave token ids --write` to fill in document identity. Night inherits the corresponding day's identity.
- `meta.baseId` is the main's root `$id` in named profile (including its night) output, and `null` in main (including its night) output. It is a payload v2 addition, and `version` stays fixed at `2`; if the Sketch plugin strictly validates the legacy `meta` field set, confirm the plugin accepts `baseId` first — do not judge compatibility by the version number alone.
- Every record carries `name` and `kind`; when the token has a registered token-level `$id`, it also carries `uuid`, otherwise that field is omitted.
- `kind` has exactly three values: `color` (color tokens, corresponding to Swatches), `text` (typography tokens, corresponding to shared text styles), and `layer` (shadows, gradients, outline borders, corner dimensions, etc., corresponding to shared layer styles).
- Only syncable assets enter the manifest: plain borders, plain dimensions, transitions, and the like produce no records.
- Text records contain only font fields (`fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `kerning`), never the text color; `fontWeight` accepts only the 100–900 hundreds scale, and other values error immediately at Sketch build time, leaving CSS and JSON unaffected.
- Layer records combine fields such as `shadows`, `gradient`, `opacity`, and `corners`; `fills` and `gradient` are mutually exclusive within one record.
- Records follow the token order in the theme files; renaming or changing anything besides `path` does not disturb the order.

Asset names must be unique within one manifest: when two tokens produce exactly the same name, the build errors. Slashes in names are plain characters, and overlapping prefixes are not conflicts — `shadow` and `shadow/elevation-1` can coexist.

Color positions in layer records always carry `#RRGGBBAA` HEX8 color snapshots with no Swatch binding; color assets in the same manifest still carry `uuid` by their own `$id` for Sync Token adoption. Details: [Colors and typography](/design-token/color-typography).

## composite

`composite` merges a group's direct child tokens into one component object. Suited to component variants such as buttons and cards.

```yaml
component:
  button:
    outline:
      $extensions:
        composite: true
      fill:
        $value: "{theme.color.surface}"
      border:
        $value: "{theme.color.primary}"
      radius:
        $value: "9999px"
```

Rules:

- `composite` is written on the group's `$extensions`.
- Direct children of a composite group must all be tokens; further group nesting is not allowed.
- JSON/JSONC/md-yml output merges into an object.
- Sketch output no longer maps composites to component style fields; component logic will be designed separately later.

pages.title: Profile and Night model
pages.description: Understand identity, overrides, and directory relationships of base, Day profiles, and Night overlays.
pages.body:
## Base and profiles

`main.yaml` is the base and the project baseline. One base together with its Day profiles forms a series; different structures should use separate base workspaces.

A profile uses a closed `$config`:

```yaml
$id: dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
$config:
  base: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
$override:
  bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb:
    $value: "#1872f0"
theme:
  color:
    accent:
      $type: color
      $value: "#ff3366"
```

- `$config.base` must equal the main's registered root `$id` verbatim.
- `$override` keys are base token `$id`s, not token paths or document IDs.
- Each entry contains only `$value`; objects and arrays are replaced wholesale, with no sub-field merging.
- New tokens must not collide with existing paths; existing groups must not re-declare metadata.
- New token types must be determinable from the profile itself.
- A profile cannot delete base tokens, change existing types, or modify existing extensions.

Reference expressions survive profile merging until the reference resolution stage; they are not materialized in advance.

## Directories and base location

Explicit `-f` does not depend on fixed directory names:

```text
main.yaml
profiles/mobile.yaml
themes/mobile.yaml
variants/mobile.yaml
```

All of these Day profiles are valid. Wave walks up from the profile's directory to the nearest `main.yaml`, then verifies `$config.base`.

`--profiles all` still uses the existing workspace discovery rules and does not recursively guess YAML in arbitrary directories. The legacy variant model and `--variant` parameter are unsupported, but `variants/` works as an ordinary directory name.

## Night is a path override

Night is an override file for Day, not a profile, and does not use `$override`:

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    primary:
      $value: "#93c5fd"
```

Night only overrides leaves that Day already has under `theme.color` and `theme.state`; a root `$id` is forbidden, and Day document and token identity carry over.

Default file relationship:

```text
main.yaml                 → main@night.yaml
themes/mobile.yaml        → themes/mobile@night.yaml
variants/mobile.yaml      → variants/mobile@night.yaml
```

Select the original Day source document explicitly at build time:

```bash
wave token build -f ./main.yaml --night
wave token build -f ./themes/mobile.yaml --night
```

A missing or generally invalid overlay warns and is skipped; identity violations fail.

## Related tasks

- Create a profile: [Create a workspace and profiles](/design-token/create)
- Create an overlay: [Create a Night overlay](/design-token/night)
- Check structure: [Check a token workspace](/design-token/doctor)
- Check contrast: [Check WCAG contrast](/design-token/wcag)
- Maintain identity: [Maintain token identity](/design-token/ids)

pages.title: Built-in resources
pages.description: Browse, update, and inspect Wave's design-token reference resources.
pages.body:
## Browse resources

```bash
wave token show
wave token show palette
wave token show dimension
wave token show tailwindcss
wave token show leonardo --format yaml
wave token show wave --format json
```

| `--format` | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `flat-json` | Flat key-value, the default |
| `json` | Nested JSON |
| `yaml` | Raw YAML |

Resources only participate in reference resolution; they do not directly determine output content.

## Update the cache

```bash
wave token update
wave token update tailwindcss
wave token update tailwindcss --version 4
wave token update leonardo
```

Without a name, updates all supported resources.

## Show status

```bash
wave token status
```

Status includes cache, state, and config paths, plus the Tailwind CSS and Leonardo cache state.

## Common resources

| Resource | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tailwindcss` | Tailwind palette |
| `leonardo` | Leonardo light/dark palettes |
| `wave` | Wave's built-in dimension system |

pages.title: Asset compression
pages.description: Compress PNG, JPG, SVG, and GIF assets, and control preview, output, and writing.
pages.body:
## Preview compression

```bash
wave compress -f ./assets --dry-run
```

The input can be a file or a directory; the default is the current directory. `--dry-run` shows the real compression results without writing files.

## Write output

```bash
wave compress -f ./assets --yes
wave compress -f ./assets --output ./optimized --yes
```

By default, output goes to `wave-compress/` under the input directory; source files are never overwritten. `--yes` only skips the confirmation; overwriting existing output still requires `--force`.

## Scope and quality

```bash
wave compress -f ./assets --type png --type jpg --recursive
wave compress -f ./assets --type png --quality 80
```

`--type` only accepts repeated flags, not comma-joined values. Supported types: `png`, `jpg`, `svg`, `gif`.

Without `--quality`, the default safe policy applies. Passing a value from 1–100 enables lossy quality mode.

## SVG icon cleanup

```bash
wave compress -f ./assets --type svg --icon --yes
```

`--icon` cleans SVG icon colors so they can be recolored through CSS.

## Toolchain

```bash
wave compress doctor
wave compress install --check
wave compress install --yes
```

Check the tools first, review the install plan, then confirm the installation.

pages.title: Motion generation
pages.description: Generate GIF or APNG from a directory of PNG frames, controlling format, output, and overwriting.
pages.body:
## Generate motion

```bash
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif
wave motion -f ./frames --format apng
```

The input directory needs at least two PNG frames. Non-interactive environments must pass `--format gif|apng` explicitly; in a TTY, omitting the format opens an interactive choice.

## Output

```bash
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --output ./loading.gif
wave motion -f ./frames --format apng --output ./loading.png
```

By default, output goes to `wave-mg/` under the frames directory; the file name contains the frames directory name and the FPS. Existing output is rejected by default; confirm first, then use `--force`.

Preview the plan only:

```bash
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --dry-run
```

## Encoding parameters

```bash
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --fps 24 --quality 80 --loop forever
```

| Parameter | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--fps <n>` | 24 |
| `-q, --quality <n>` | 80 |
| `--loop <mode>` | `forever`; also supports `once` |

The command never modifies the source frames.

## Toolchain and frame checks

```bash
wave motion doctor
wave motion doctor -f ./frames
wave motion install --check
wave motion install --yes
```

`motion doctor` accepts an optional `-f` PNG frames directory to check the frame input at the same time.

pages.title: Workspace creation
pages.description: Create design project directories from local configuration, controlling target location and existing content.
pages.body:
## Create a workspace

```bash
wave workspace
```

The command asks for project name, type, version, and tags per the configuration, then creates the directory structure and README. No `create` subcommand is needed.

Preview the plan only:

```bash
wave workspace --dry-run
```

Skip the write confirmation:

```bash
wave workspace --yes
```

## Target location

```bash
wave workspace --output ./my-project --yes
```

`--output` points at the final workspace directory, not a parent. The logical project name still comes from the interactive answers.

Existing targets are rejected by default. With `--force`, Wave only overwrites the README and placeholder files this run would generate, keeps other files in the directory, and never deletes content recursively. Plain files and symlinks as targets are still rejected.

## Configuration file

Default path:

```text
~/.config/wave/workspace.yaml
```

Use another configuration:

```bash
WAVE_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=/path/to/workspace.yaml wave workspace
```

When the file is missing, built-in defaults apply. `WAVE_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` affects workspace only, not the token resource cache.

The command asks for project name, type, version, and tags per the configuration, then creates the directory structure and README. No `create` subcommand is needed.

Preview the plan only:

```bash
wave workspace --dry-run
```

Skip the write confirmation:

```bash
wave workspace --yes
```

## Target location

```bash
wave workspace --output ./my-project --yes
```

`--output` points at the final workspace directory, not a parent. The logical project name still comes from the interactive answers.

Existing targets are rejected by default. With `--force`, Wave only overwrites the README and placeholder files this run would generate, keeps other files in the directory, and never deletes content recursively. Plain files and symlinks as targets are still rejected.

## Configuration file

Default path:

```text
~/.config/wave/workspace.yaml
```

Use another configuration:

```bash
WAVE_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=/path/to/workspace.yaml wave workspace
```

When the file is missing, built-in defaults apply. `WAVE_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` affects workspace only, not the token resource cache.

pages.body:
## Common commands

```bash
wave token
wave compress -f ./assets --dry-run
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --dry-run
wave workspace --dry-run
```

`wave token` builds the current directory's `main.yaml` by default. Compression, motion, and workspace commands also run their tasks directly, with no extra `run`, `gif`, or `create` subcommand.

## Design Token

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `wave token build` | Generate token outputs |
| `wave token new` | Create a token workspace |
| `wave token new profile <name>` | Create a profile from a registered base |
| `wave token new night` | Create a Night overlay from a Day main or profile |
| `wave token doctor` | Check workspace, resources, and identity |
| `wave token wcag` | Check color contrast |
| `wave token ids` | Report or write back document and token identity |
| `wave token migrate extensions` | Migrate legacy `$extensions` syntax |
| `wave token show` | Browse built-in resources |
| `wave token update [name]` | Update the resource cache |
| `wave token status` | Show resource cache status |

The bare `wave token` command equals `wave token build`. `migrate` has no default migration target; `extensions` must be written explicitly.

## Asset toolchain

```bash
wave compress doctor
wave compress install --check
wave motion doctor -f ./frames
wave motion install --check
```

`--check` only shows the install plan. Add `--yes` only after confirming.

## Global commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `wave doctor` | Check the local runtime and toolchain |
| `wave install` | Review or run recommended tool installation |
| `wave workspace` | Create a design project workspace |
| `wave manual` | Launch the visual web manual |
| `wave version` | Show the version |

## Get the manual

`--help` gives concise help. `-m, --manual` prints structured Markdown for the current command scope, suited for agents:

```bash
wave -m
wave token -m
wave token new -m
wave token new night -m
wave token migrate extensions -m
```

Documentation mode runs no builds, creation, compression, or encoding, and never starts a web server.

pages.title: Configuration paths
pages.description: Locate Wave's workspace configuration, resource cache, and default output locations.
pages.body:
## Workspace configuration

```text
~/.config/wave/workspace.yaml
```

Override the path:

```bash
WAVE_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=/path/to/workspace.yaml wave workspace
```

## Resource cache

```bash
wave token status
```

Output includes cache, state, and config paths, plus the Tailwind CSS and Leonardo cache state.

## Token output

Configured in `main.yaml`:

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./dist
    platform: [json, css]
```

Command-line override of the output directory for one run:

```bash
wave token build -f ./main.yaml --output ./dist
```

The platform list is maintained only in `$config`; there is no CLI `--platform`.

## Profile and Night output

Default locations:

```text
profiles/<name>.yaml
<Day directory>/<stem>@night.yaml
```

Both accept `--output` for a custom file. Custom locations do not widen implicit discovery; see the corresponding creation manuals for how they are consumed later.

## Compress output

```text
<input>/wave-compress/
```

Override the output directory:

```bash
wave compress -f ./assets --output ./optimized --yes
```

## Motion output

```text
<frames>/wave-mg/<frames-name>@<fps>fps.gif
<frames>/wave-mg/<frames-name>@<fps>fps.png
```

Use `--output` to specify the complete output file path.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Use the right check entry points to locate environment, source document, write, and toolchain issues.
pages.body:
## Where to start

```bash
wave --help
wave -m
wave doctor --status
```

`--help` shows concise command help, `-m` prints the Markdown manual for the current scope, and `doctor` checks the local toolchain.

## main.yaml not found

`wave token` reads the current directory's `main.yaml` by default. For a new project, run first:

```bash
wave token new
wave token
```

For an existing project, use `-f`:

```bash
wave token build -f /path/to/main.yaml
wave token build -f /path/to/workspace-directory
```

## main.yaml missing $config

The entry document must contain a valid `$config`:

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./dist
    platform: [json, css]
```

Use `wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml` to check structure and resources.

## Profile fails to build

```bash
wave token doctor -f /path/to/profile.yaml
wave token ids -f /path/to/main.yaml
```

Check:

- The profile sits in the base main's directory or a subdirectory of it.
- `$config.base` equals the main's original root `$id`.
- `$override` uses registered token `$id`s.
- New token types can be determined from the profile itself.

To create a profile, register the base first, then run `wave token new profile <name> -f ./main.yaml`.

## Night is not built

Confirm the overlay sits next to the Day source document and is named `<stem>@night.yaml`. Then select the original Day source explicitly:

```bash
wave token build -f /path/to/day-or-profile.yaml --night
```

Custom `--output` locations are not auto-discovered. Profile Night cannot be consumed by building main alone.

## Output already exists

New source documents and motion output never overwrite existing targets by default. Preview the plan with `--dry-run` first, then add `--force` after confirming the overwrite:

```bash
wave token new night -f ./main.yaml --force
wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --force
```

`--yes` only skips the confirmation; it does not grant overwrite permission.

## Missing tools

```bash
wave compress doctor
wave compress install --check
wave motion doctor
wave motion install --check
```

Run the matching `install --yes` only after confirming the install plan.

## Command does not exist

The only token entry today is `wave token`; motion has no `mg`. Common migrations:

| Old form | Current form |
| --- | --- |
| `wave dt build` | `wave token build` |
| `wave dt init` | `wave token new` |
| `wave night` | `wave token new night` |
| `wave compress run` | `wave compress` |
| `wave motion gif` | `wave motion --format gif` |
| `wave workspace create` | `wave workspace` |
| `--out` | `--output` |

pages.title: Installation and toolchain
pages.description: Install development dependencies, and check or install the local tools Wave needs.
pages.body:
## Purpose

Wave itself runs on Bun, project dependencies are managed with pnpm, and the local toolchain comes from mise and system tools. Wave does not bundle image compression or motion encoding tools into the CLI.

## Development environment

```bash
mise install
pnpm install
pnpm dev -- --version
```

## Check the environment

```bash
wave doctor
wave doctor --status
wave doctor --json
```

`doctor` checks the Wave runtime environment and recommended tools. Module commands also provide standalone checks:

```bash
wave compress doctor
wave motion doctor
```

## Review the install plan

```bash
wave install --check
wave compress install --check
wave motion install --check
```

## Run the installation

After confirming the install plan, add `--yes` to the matching install command to run the installation. Install commands invoke the project's mise tasks. When mise is missing, Wave tells you to install mise first.

## Tool groups

| Module | Local tools |
| --- | --- |
| compress | `oxipng`, `pngquant`, `svgo`, `gifsicle`, `jpegtran` or `mozjpeg` |
| motion | `gifski`, `apngasm` |

pages.title: Design token overview
pages.description: Use the token module to build outputs, create source documents, check quality, and maintain resources.
pages.body:
## Default build

From a directory containing `main.yaml`, run:

```bash
wave token
```

It is equivalent to:

```bash
wave token build
```

Output platforms are decided by `$config.parameter.platform` or parameter groups in `main.yaml`. The CLI no longer provides `--platform`; change the configuration to adjust platforms.

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./dist
    platform: [json, css]
```

## Command groups

| Group | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| Build | `build` |
| Create | `new`, `new profile`, `new night` |
| Check | `doctor`, `wcag` |
| Identity | `ids` |
| Migrate | `migrate extensions` |
| Resources | `show`, `update`, `status` |

Use `-m` to get the full Markdown manual at any level:

```bash
wave token -m
wave token new -m
wave token new night -m
```

## Source document input

`-f, --file` selects the source document for the operation:

```bash
wave token build
wave token build -f ./themes/acme
wave token build -f ./themes/acme/main.yaml
wave token build -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml
```

Rules:

- Omitting `-f`: reads `./main.yaml`.
- A directory input: reads the `main.yaml` inside it.
- A `main.yaml` input: processes the default profile.
- Any other Day YAML input: processes that profile and locates the base `main.yaml` from the nearest ancestor directory.
- An `@night.yaml` input: rejected. Night is not a Day source document.

Directories may be named `profiles`, `themes`, `variants`, or anything else. Explicit `-f` does not depend on directory names.

## Build scope

```bash
# Build main only
wave token build -f ./themes/acme

# Build one named profile only
wave token build -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml

# Build main and all named profiles via the workspace discovery rules
wave token build -f ./themes/acme --profiles all

# Consume the Night overlay at its conventional location at the same time
wave token build -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml --night
```

`--profiles all` only works with a main file or directory; it cannot combine with a single profile file. It does not recursively guess YAML in every directory.

## Output

All token build outputs accept `-o, --output` to override the configured output directory:

```bash
wave token build -f ./main.yaml --output ./dist

pages.title: Create a workspace and profiles
pages.description: Use token new to create a base workspace or a profile from a registered base.
pages.body:
## Create a token workspace

```bash
wave token new
```

By default, creates a `main.yaml` with `$config` in the current directory. Target a different directory:

```bash
wave token new --output ./my-tokens
```

The target is `./my-tokens/main.yaml`. The directory itself may already exist, but when the target `main.yaml` exists, replacing it requires `--force`.

Preview the plan only:

```bash
wave token new --output ./my-tokens --dry-run
```

## Create a named profile

First register the base document and all token identities:

```bash
wave token ids -f ./main.yaml
wave token ids --write -f ./main.yaml
```

Then create the profile:

```bash
wave token new profile mobile -f ./main.yaml
```

The default output is `<workspace>/profiles/mobile.yaml`. Profile names are lowercased and ASCII spaces become `_`; illegal names, duplicate names, and invalid output file names are rejected.

## Profile custom output

Use `-o, --output` to specify the file:

```bash
wave token new profile mobile -f ./main.yaml --output ./themes/mobile.yaml
```

The output file's stem must equal the normalized profile name. For example, `mobile` can only be written as `mobile.yaml`, not `desktop.yaml`.

If the output sits in the base `main.yaml`'s directory or a subdirectory, it builds directly:

```bash
wave token build -f ./themes/mobile.yaml
```

If the output goes outside the base directory tree, Wave cannot locate main from `$config.base` alone. Move the same `mobile.yaml` into a directory tree the base can discover, then build it through `-f`. `--profiles all` does not scan arbitrary external locations.

## Write safety

Both creation commands follow:

- Target missing: create the target file.
- Target exists: reject and leave the bytes untouched.
- `--force`: overwrite only the target file selected this run.
- `--dry-run`: print the full plan without creating directories or files.

Same-name profile conflicts and target file conflicts are checked separately. A custom path cannot bypass a same-name profile conflict; `--force` allows replacement only when the conflict is the current output target itself.

## What gets generated

A profile carries its own document `$id`, a `$config.base` pointing at the base, and an `$override` snapshot of base token source values. Reference expressions stay as written and are not materialized in advance.

After creation, delete redundant overrides that do not need to be pinned so those tokens keep following the base. For Night, see [Create a Night overlay](/design-token/night).

pages.title: Create a Night overlay
pages.description: Generate a Night overlay from a Day main or Day profile, controlling output location and overwrite behavior.
pages.body:
## Purpose

Generate a path-based Night overlay from an existing Day source document:

```bash
wave token new night
wave token new night -f ./themes/acme
wave token new night -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml
```

The command completes base/profile merging, resource loading, and reference resolution, then derives Night from the resolved Day colors. It never modifies the Day source file.

## Input

| Input | Day source document |
| --- | --- |
| `-f` omitted | `./main.yaml` |
| `-f <directory>` | `<directory>/main.yaml` |
| `-f <main.yaml>` | The specified main |
| `-f <other-day.yaml>` | The specified profile |

Profiles may live in `profiles`, `themes`, `variants`, or any other directory. Wave searches ancestor directories for the nearest base `main.yaml` and verifies the profile's `$config.base`.

Do not pass `@night.yaml`, resource files, or standalone YAML without a base.

## Default output

The output file sits next to the Day source document:

```text
main.yaml                 → main@night.yaml
themes/mobile.yaml        → themes/mobile@night.yaml
variants/mobile.yaml      → variants/mobile@night.yaml
```

The fixed naming lets the following command find the overlay automatically:

```bash
wave token build -f <Day source document> --night
```

## Custom output

Use `-o, --output` to specify another YAML file:

```bash
wave token new night -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml --output ./drafts/mobile-night.yaml
```

Custom locations are not discovered by the default build. To consume them:

1. Move the content back to `mobile@night.yaml` next to the Day source document.
2. Run the original Day profile's build:

```bash
wave token build -f ./themes/acme/themes/mobile.yaml --night
```

Building main alone never consumes a profile's Night.

## Overwrite and preview

When the target exists, it is rejected by default and the original file stays untouched:

```bash
wave token new night -f ./main.yaml
```

To confirm the overwrite:

```bash
wave token new night -f ./main.yaml --force
```

Preview the generation plan without writing files:

```bash
wave token new night -f ./main.yaml --dry-run
```

`--force` overwrites only the target overlay; it never touches the Day document, base, or other files. Directory and symlink targets are still rejected.

## Appearance parameters

```bash
wave token new night --scene candle-light
wave token new night --luminance 0.55
wave token new night --luminance-ev high
```

| Parameter | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `--scene` | `moon`, `night-light`, `night`, `candle-light`, `sunset` |
| `--luminance` | Primary Night luminance dial from 0 to 1 |
| `--luminance-ev` | `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max` |

Priority:

```text
--luminance > --luminance-ev > $config.night > built-in defaults
```

Scene uses `--scene > $config.night.scene > night`. `--luminance` controls luminance, not chroma; the legacy `--chroma` and `--chroma-ev` flags are no longer accepted.

## Content contract

The overlay contains only `$value` overrides for paths that already exist under `theme.color` and `theme.state`, and never writes a root `$id`. Day and Night share the theme identity; Sketch distinguishes the appearance through `meta.mode=night`.

After generation, run:

```bash
wave token doctor -f <Day source document>
wave token wcag -f <Day source document> --night
wave token build -f <Day source document> --night
```

pages.title: Migrate token source documents
pages.description: Use the token migrate command group to migrate legacy extension fields and control source-file write-back.
pages.body:
## Command group

`wave token migrate` has no default migration target. Currently supported:

```bash
wave token migrate extensions -f ./main.yaml
```

`extensions` migrates the legacy `$extensions` Sketch family syntax to `platform.sketch`. It does not migrate legacy standalone profiles and never changes token values or output platforms.

## Report and write back

By default, only a change report is printed:

```bash
wave token migrate extensions -f ./main.yaml
```

After reviewing the report, write back to main and the Day profiles in the workspace:

```bash
wave token migrate extensions -f ./main.yaml --write
```

`-f` accepts the base `main.yaml` or the directory containing it. Do not use resources, Night overlays, or single profiles as entry points for this workspace migration command.

Write-back modifies only source YAML within the confirmed scope. Review the report before running and make sure no unrelated changes are included.

## Get the manual for the current scope

```bash
wave token migrate -m
wave token migrate extensions -m
```

The first explains the command group and migration targets; the second gives the concrete usage of `extensions`.

pages.title: Check a token workspace
pages.description: Use token doctor to check structure, resources, identity, and existing output directories.
pages.body:
## Usage

```bash
wave token doctor
wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml
wave token doctor -f ./themes/mobile.yaml
```

`-f` accepts a main, a directory containing main, or a Day profile in any directory. A default main input checks main plus named profiles under the existing discovery rules; an explicit profile file checks only the selected target.

## Check scope

- main/profile structure and base linkage.
- `$override` hits and redundant overrides.
- Document and token identity conflicts.
- All resources declared by the currently selected targets, including declarations that are never referenced.
- Migratable legacy `theme.dimension` usage.

Redundant overrides produce info only and do not change the success state. Structure errors, identity conflicts, and invalid resources exit non-zero.

## Output directory check

```bash
wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml --output ./dist
```

`--output` checks an existing output directory. The check fails when the directory is missing or the path is not a directory. No output is created here and no build runs.

## Output modes

```bash

pages.title: Check WCAG contrast
pages.description: Use token wcag to check color contrast of main, profiles, or Night.
pages.body:
## Declare check items

Declare at the root of `main.yaml`:

```yaml
doctor:
  wcagPairs:
    primary-on-surface:
      foreground: "{theme.color.primary}"
      background: "{theme.color.surface}"
```

Each pair must contain `foreground` and `background`. Both values must be alias strings pointing at resolved color tokens.

The `doctor` root key does not participate in token output.

## Run the check

```bash
wave token wcag
wave token wcag -f ./main.yaml
wave token wcag -f ./themes/mobile.yaml
wave token wcag -f ./themes/mobile.yaml --night
```

`-f` selects a main or a Day profile directly; there is no `[scope]` or `--profile`. `--night` reads the conventional overlay next to the current Day source document.

## Scoring

| Dimension | AA | AAA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal Text | 4.5 | 7 |
| Large Text | 3 | 4.5 |
| UI Components | 3 | No AAA judgment |

Thresholds use the unrounded ratio. Red scores are reporting only and do not block the command; invalid schema, unresolved references, non-color inputs, or unsynthesized alpha return non-zero.

## How it differs from other checks

`wave token doctor` checks workspace health and does not run WCAG. `wave doctor` only checks the local toolchain.

pages.title: Maintain token identity
pages.description: Use token ids to report or write back `$id`s of main, Day profiles, and tokens.
pages.body:
## Report only by default

```bash
wave token ids -f ./main.yaml
```

Reports document identity, registered and unregistered tokens, empty slots, non-canonical forms, and cross-file conflicts, without modifying files.

## Write identity back

After reviewing the report, run:

```bash
wave token ids --write -f ./main.yaml
```

The write scope covers main and Day profiles under the existing discovery rules. Missing or empty identity slots get filled; existing document root IDs are never re-issued. `$override` and Night files are excluded from writing.

Writing requires a clean Git worktree by default. Only when you confirm keeping current uncommitted changes, use:

```bash
wave token ids --write --allow-dirty -f ./main.yaml
```

## Identity rules

- main and each Day profile may declare their own document `$id` at the root.
- Token `$id` lives on the token; groups do not declare `$id`.
- Absent means unregistered; `null` or a blank string means a reserved slot.
- Token identity must be unique within one theme.
- Night must not carry a root `$id`; it inherits the Day identity.

A profile's `$config.base` must equal the main's registered root `$id`. When a profile exists but main is unregistered, the base does not match, or token IDs conflict, ids refuses to write any file. Do not bypass conflicts by re-issuing main's identity.

## Create follow-up content

After registering the base, create a profile:

```bash
wave token new profile mobile -f ./main.yaml
```

See [Create a workspace and profiles](/design-token/create) for profile creation prerequisites and output rules.

pages.title: main.yaml syntax
pages.description: Reference for `$config`, parameterGroup, token structure, and `theme` top-level keys in main.yaml.
pages.body:
## main.yaml

`main.yaml` declares both `$config` and token content. Fully self-contained tokens do not need to declare resources:

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./build
    platform: [json, css]
theme:
  color:
    primary:
      $type: color
      $value: "#2563eb"
```

When tokens reference external values, declare the dependencies through `$config.resource`:

```yaml
$schema: "https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/"

$config:
  theme: example
  resource:
    palette:
      - tailwindcss
    dimension:
      - wave
  parameter:
    outputDir: ./build
    platform:
      - json
      - css
    colorSpace: hex
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    primary:
      $description: Brand primary color
      $value: "{tailwindcss.color.indigo.600}"
    onPrimary:
      $value: "#ffffff"
  radius:
    card:
      $type: dimension
      $value: "12px"
```

`$config` supports:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `theme` | Theme name, also the output file name prefix |
| `resource.palette` | Optional; palette resources, given as a non-empty string or a non-empty string array |
| `resource.dimension` | Optional; dimension resources, given as a non-empty string or a non-empty string array |
| `resource.custom` | Optional; custom resource files, given as a non-empty string or a non-empty string array |
| `parameter.outputDir` | Non-empty output directory |
| `parameter.platform` | Non-empty array; supports `json`, `jsonc`, `css`, `sketch`, `md-yml` |
| `parameter.filterLayer` | Integer ≥ 0; skips the first N path layers when outputting keys |
| `parameter.colorSpace` | Supports `hex`, `oklch`, `srgb`, `hsl` |
| `parameterGroup.<name>` | Additional output parameter sets; fields match `parameter` |

`$config` is a closed structure. Unknown fields, wrong types, empty strings, or invalid enum values fail the build and show the field path in the error.

Build only requires every reference in the token graph to resolve uniquely. Missing, broken, or duplicate resource declarations that are never referenced do not block the build; `wave token doctor` strictly checks every declaration on the current target.

## parameterGroup

`parameterGroup` builds several output sets at once. `parameter` provides the defaults and each group overrides fields of the same name. A group accepts exactly the same fields as `parameter`.

```yaml
$config:
  theme: example
  resource:
    palette: tailwindcss
    dimension: wave
  parameter:
    colorSpace: hex
    filterLayer: 1
  parameterGroup:
    css:
      outputDir: ./build/css
      platform: [css]
    sketch:
      outputDir: ./build/sketch
      platform: [sketch]
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    primary:
      $value: "{tailwindcss.color.indigo.600}"
```

Wave expands `parameterGroup`; each group produces one pass. `--output` overrides the output directories of these passes and does not change a group's platform, `filterLayer`, or `colorSpace`. The platform list is no longer overridden from the CLI; adjust `parameter` or the relevant parameter group in the configuration.

Wave checks every output path of the whole build before writing, including default, named profile, valid night, and each parameter group. If two passes would write the same file, the build fails immediately and existing files stay untouched; for example, one group outputs `[json, css]` while another outputs `[json]` into the same directory, and they fail because the JSON paths overlap. An invalid night still warns and is skipped, and does not join the path check.

## Token syntax

Wave uses DTCG-style structure:

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    $type: color
    surface:
      $value: "#ffffff"
    text:
      $value: "{theme.color.surface}"
```

Common fields:

| Field | Location | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$type` | group or token | Token type, inheritable by child nodes |
| `$value` | token | Token value |
| `$description` | group or token | Emitted into jsonc/css comments |
| `$id` | main/profile root, token | Identity field, see the next section |
| `$deprecated` | token | Marks deprecation |
| `$ref` | token | JSON Pointer reference, e.g. `#/theme/color/primary/$value` |
| `$extends` | group | Inherits another group, format `{theme.group.path}` |
| `$extensions` | group or token | Wave extension fields |

## The identity field $id

`$id` is Wave's identity field so that Sketch sync still recognizes tokens after they are renamed or moved. It has two levels:

- Document level: main and every day profile may declare their own `$id` at the root, delivered as `meta.themeId` in Sketch output. The field is optional; when declared it must be a non-empty string. Night files must not declare a root `$id` and inherit the day document identity.
- Token level: written on the token. Three states: absent means unregistered; an empty value (`null` or a blank string) means a reserved slot; a non-empty string registers the identity. Token identity must be unique within one theme; groups cannot declare `$id`.

Use `wave token ids` to maintain both levels: by default it only prints a dry-run report, and `--write` writes back document root identity plus new token identity for main and day profiles. Missing or empty identity slots get filled and existing document root IDs are never re-issued; `$override` and night files are excluded from writing. Writing requires a clean Git worktree by default; to keep current uncommitted changes, pass `--allow-dirty` explicitly.

A profile's `$config.base` must equal the main's registered root `$id` from before the run. Whenever a profile exists while main is unregistered, or any profile's base is missing or mismatched, ids refuses to write any file. Register main in a base directory that has no profiles yet, then create profiles. Details: [Profiles and Night](/design-token/quality-theming).

`$id` does not affect token values in json, jsonc, css, or md-yml; Sketch uses it only for asset association and never changes keys.

```bash
wave token ids -f ./main.yaml
wave token ids --write -f ./main.yaml
```

```yaml
$id: 6f1c2a54b7d84e0f9a1c32d45e6b70f8

$config:
  theme: example

theme:
  color:
    primary:
      $id: 0f8e6d5c4b3a29180f7e6d5c4b3a2918
      $type: color
      $value: "#2563eb"
```

Wave supports every standard DTCG 2025.10 `$type`:

| Category | `$type` |
| --- | --- |
| Basic values | `color`, `dimension`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `duration`, `cubicBezier`, `number`, `strokeStyle` |
| Composite values | `border`, `transition`, `shadow`, `gradient`, `typography` |

`opacity` is not a standard `$type`. Use a `number` token for transparency; `inheritColor.property.opacity` and `$extensions.platform.sketch.property.opacity` are Wave extension fields, documented under "Extensions and output". Unknown custom `$type`s produce a warning; JSON/JSONC keep the value, md-yml keeps YAML-safe values, CSS emits scalars only, and custom objects or arrays fail the CSS build.

## Dimension syntax

The DTCG standard dimension uses an object with units limited to `px` or `rem`:

```yaml
space:
  $type: dimension
  $value:
    value: 8
    unit: px
```

Wave also accepts these shorthands:

```yaml
spaceNumber:
  $type: dimension
  $value: 8
spaceString:
  $type: dimension
  $value: "8"
spaceLength:
  $type: dimension
  $value: "0.5rem"
spaceObject:
  $type: dimension
  $value:
    value: 8
```

The shorthands also support `pt`, `em`, and `%`. Unit-less values default to `px` in JSON, JSONC, and CSS, so both `8` and `{ value: 8 }` output `"8px"`. These forms are Wave input capabilities, not the DTCG standard dimension; when Sketch native numeric properties cannot express a unit, the build stops instead of converting silently.

## Typed references

A complete-token alias inherits the target token's type; references inside composite values must point at matching standard types:

```yaml
theme:
  color:
    primary:
      $type: color
      $value: "#1872f0"
  radius:
    small:
      $type: dimension
      $value: 4
  border:
    dashed:
      $type: strokeStyle
      $value:
        dashArray: [4, 8]
        lineCap: butt
    control:
      $type: border
      $value:
        color: "{theme.color.primary}"
        width: "{theme.radius.small}"
        style: "{theme.border.dashed}"
    controlAlias:
      $value: "{theme.border.control}"
```

You can also reference a complete value with `$ref: "#/theme/border/control/$value"`. Type mismatches, unresolved references, or composites missing standard fields report the token path and fail the build.

## `theme` top-level keys

Top-level keys under `theme` express token purpose and also shape CSS and Sketch output. New projects should prefer these roots:

| Key | Purpose | Common `$type` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | Brand, semantic, text, background, and stroke colors | `color` |
| `state` | Interaction state values such as hover, pressed, disabled | `number` |
| `shadow` | Drop, elevation, and smooth shadows | `shadow` |
| `gradient` | Gradients, mask gradients, smooth gradients | `gradient` |
| `border` | Stroke widths, stroke styles, outline tokens | `dimension`, `border` |
| `radius` | Corner radii and component radii | `dimension`, `number` |
| `font` | Font, size, weight, line-height, and letter-spacing combinations | `typography` |

CSS output treats only `color`, `state`, `shadow`, `gradient`, `border`, `radius`, and `font` as public roots. `theme.dimension` remains only for legacy project compatibility and is no longer a recommended public output root; put dimensions, opacity, and curves into the root matching their purpose, or keep using them as `$config.resource.dimension` reference resources.

References come in two forms:

```yaml
primary:
  $value: "{tailwindcss.color.indigo.600}"

secondary:
  $ref: "#/theme/color/primary/$value"
```

## Compatibility fields

| Field | Status | Replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currentColor` | deprecated | `inheritColor` |

New documents and new projects should not keep using compatibility fields.
